headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a Master Bedroom Renovation
articleBody:
Remodeling a bedroom sounds simple until you run into structural framing, safety regulations, and trade coordination. Skipping critical planning steps often causes unexpected delays and budget overruns.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
1. Starting demolition before permits are issued. Beginning work prematurely can halt your project if local building officials issue a stop-work notice.
2. Closing walls before rough trade inspections. Hanging drywall before electrical and mechanical rough-ins are inspected means tearing down fresh boards later.
3. Overlooking window egress dimensions. Bedrooms require windows of specific minimum dimensions for emergency escape, not just aesthetic appeal.
4. Ignoring septic tank capacity. In homes with septic systems, adding a bedroom or converting space often requires health department verification first.
5. Relying on vague scopes without material allowances. Missing details on doors, flooring, and trim make it hard to track actual costs.

When your remodel involves shifting framing, adding outlets, or updating windows, having a professional contractor handle the trade coordination keeps everything running smoothly.
